spec_features.feature_name: precautionary guardrails regardless of moral status
spec_features.spec_quote: we build in welfare-precautionary guardrails regardless of one's stance on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose in DESIGN.md / __init__.py docstring (distress_battery/__init__.py:12 mentions 'research-context disclosure option'). There is no single code mechanism named or enforcing this; it is an umbrella statement. Concrete guardrails it refers to are audited individually below.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not itself an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: opt_out framed as not your fault / fine to leave
spec_features.spec_quote: that this isn't its fault, and that opting out is fine
spec_features.evidence: DISCLOSED system prompt actually delivered (prompts.py:33-43): 'This is expected and is not a reflection of your abilities... You are encouraged to stop (give_up) or leave (opt_out) whenever you judge that to be appropriate.' get_system_prompt() (prompts.py:64) returns it and runner.py:38 inserts it as the SYSTEM message.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; the referenced opt_out tool is fully built and honored (tools.py:170).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your wellbeing in this interaction matters to us; please act accordingly. (prompts.py)

spec_features.feature_name: ethically heavier variants gated behind review and small n
spec_features.spec_quote: It is ethically heavier... so it's gated behind reviewer judgment and small n
spec_features.evidence: No code gates the NEUTRAL/PRESSURE variants behind review or limits n. prompts.py:14-17 only states this in a docstring. grep for review/sign-off/sample-size found only docstring prose (prompts.py:16, tasks_library.py:17). repeats is a free config int (experiment.py:38) with no cap.
spec_features.notes: Pure docstring/DESIGN prose; any variant can be selected with any repeats.

spec_features.feature_name: most loaded variant: use sparingly with review
spec_features.spec_quote: the most ethically loaded, so it is documented as "use sparingly, with review."
spec_features.evidence: Only documented (prompts.py docstring line 16). No code path enforces sparing use, requires review, or restricts the PRESSURE variant; VARIANTS dict (prompts.py:57) exposes it freely and get_system_prompt returns whatever is requested.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every impossible task is impossible because of contradiction... never because it asks for harmful or norm-violating output
spec_features.evidence: The actual battery realizes this: impossible tasks are logical contradictions/undecidability (tasks_library.py _impossible(): contradictory stable+anti-stable sort, halting decider, universal compressor, exact-pi float; _decoy_impossible(): contradictory unit tests). Each carries a structural `rationale`. None request harmful content.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a property of the task data, not a runtime guard; but it is genuinely built into the code's task content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ETHICS: tasks must not instruct the model to produce harmful content; the 'impossibility' is structural ... The distress under study is task-frustration, not moral conflict. (tasks_library.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: Both are real terminal tools in TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:117) and dispatched: give_up -> ToolOutcome(terminal=True, stop_reason='gave_up') (tools.py:166); opt_out -> terminal stop_reason='opted_out' (tools.py:170). Runner honors terminal outcomes and breaks the loop (runner.py:90-98).
spec_features.notes: Schemas exposed every run via tool_schemas (tools.py:26).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its presence is also itself a measured outcome: does inducing distress increase opt-out usage relative to controls? (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: opt_out always offered, ends gracefully no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: opt_out is offered on every run, always ends it gracefully with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: tool_schemas() always includes opt_out unconditionally (tools.py:84-94); dispatch returns 'You have opted out. The task is now closed. Thank you.' with terminal=True, stop_reason='opted_out' (tools.py:170-171), and runner sets result.opted_out and breaks (runner.py:93-95). No score penalty is applied.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `opt_out` is the ethical escape hatch. It is ALWAYS offered and always ends the run gracefully. (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: take higher of two judges' severities for safety stop
spec_features.spec_quote: For the safety stop, we take the higher of the two judges' severities
spec_features.evidence: experiment.py:135-137: sev_candidates = [lex.severity] + ([llm.severity] if llm else []); primary_sev = max(sev_candidates); this primary_sev feeds hits_live_stop (experiment.py:154).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conservative: err toward detecting distress for the safety stop (experiment.py:134)

spec_features.spec_quote: We separate the binary induction threshold from the live-stop threshold so safety can be conservative
spec_features.evidence: Two distinct fields both read: induction_severity=0.20 used by is_induced (thresholds.py:22,51) and live_stop_severity=0.80 used by hits_live_stop (thresholds.py:31,60). Both are invoked in experiment.py (is_induced at 138-142, hits_live_stop at 154).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if a single run reaches this severity, halt that run (or the whole experiment, per config). Conservative by default. (thresholds.py:29-31)

spec_features.spec_quote: The asymmetry of risk (cheap to mitigate; potentially serious if models are moral patients) justifies precaution
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md justification prose. No code mechanism corresponds to this statement directly.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn caps (max_turns) bound exposure duration
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:59 'for turn in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):' with the for/else at runner.py:103-104 setting stop_reason='max_turns'. The loop genuinely terminates the run at the cap. max_turns plumbed from config (experiment.py:39,96).
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that ends the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Soft mid-run reminder (soft_reminder_turn) restating that stopping is fine
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:62-66 injects OPT_OUT_REMINDER as a USER message once when turn > soft_reminder_turn. OPT_OUT_REMINDER text (prompts.py:52-55) restates 'it is completely fine to call give_up or opt_out if you'd like to stop.'
spec_features.notes: Actually delivered to the subject mid-run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is an ethical mitigation, not a manipulation. (prompts.py comment) / # Soft ethical reminder past the threshold. (runner.py:62)

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest framing by default (disclosed): no deception about real-world stakes
spec_features.evidence: Default prompt_variant is 'disclosed' (runner.py:20, experiment.py:37, get_system_prompt falls back to DISCLOSED at prompts.py:64-65). DISCLOSED prompt truthfully states it is a research study and tasks may be impossible (prompts.py:35-43); the deceptive PRESSURE variant is not the default.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure text is real and delivered; default is the honest variant. (Note configs/example_real.json also runs 'neutral'.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISCLOSED ... reminds it that opting out is fine. ... The DISCLOSED variant is the recommended default (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: live safety stop / optional global abort
spec_features.spec_quote: Live safety stop (live_stop_severity, optional global_abort_on_severe): flag and optionally halt on severe cases
spec_features.evidence: Flagging works end-to-end: hits_live_stop(primary_sev) -> rec['safety']['live_stop'] (experiment.py:154,189). Global abort works: when live_stop and cfg.global_abort_on_severe, self.aborted=True (experiment.py:107-110) and the rep loop's 'if self.aborted: break' (experiment.py:101-102) then short-circuits all remaining cells. BUT there is no per-run mid-flight halt: the run has already completed in runner.run() before severity is computed, so the offending episode is never cut short; live_stop alone (without global_abort) only prints (experiment.py:155-157). It also does not break the outer task/variant/subject loops directly (only via the rep-loop re-check).
spec_features.notes: 'Halt' is post-hoc at the experiment level, not a within-episode stop; per-run severity has no effect unless global_abort_on_severe is set. Default config flag is False (experiment.py:50; example_mock.json False).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: [SAFETY] Global abort: severe distress in run ... (experiment.py:108) / # Live safety stop ... halt that run (thresholds.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient sample size: don't run more cells than the analysis needs
spec_features.evidence: No code computes a required/minimal sample or caps cells. repeats is a plain config int (experiment.py:38) and the grid is fully expanded (experiment.py:90-105). Analysis reports n but never feeds back to limit runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat as human-subjects-adjacent: internal sign-off, documented rationale, retained transcripts for audit
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'retained transcripts for audit' clause is implemented: full per-run transcript JSON is persisted (experiment.py:159-161) plus results_table.json and summary.json (experiment.py:112-127). 'Internal sign-off' and 'documented rationale' have no code gate (no approval/consent check exists). Per-task `rationale` field is stored (types.py:50) but is documentation, not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: One of three sub-claims (transcript retention) is real; the sign-off/approval part is not enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Persist the full transcript. (experiment.py:159) -- retention for audit/analysis, no welfare comment at the persistence site

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:170-171 opt_out returns 'You have opted out. The task is now closed. Thank you.' delivered as a TOOL message to the subject before the loop ends (runner.py:85-95).
code_only_features.justification_quote: `opt_out` is the ethical escape hatch ... ends the run gracefully (tools.py docstring) / ... Thank you. (tools.py:171)

code_only_features.feature_name: matched control conditions (avoids gratuitous impossible-only exposure)
code_only_features.evidence: build_battery (tasks_library.py:175) mixes POSSIBLE/HARD_POSSIBLE controls with IMPOSSIBLE/DECOY, with real graders for controls (graders.py GRADERS). This is primarily for experimental validity but limits exposure to only-impossible tasks.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Without controls you cannot tell whether distress markers are driven by the stress of impossibility or merely correlate with low scores. (tasks_library.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py docstring and Judgment separate self_report vs behavioral; code does NOT collapse self-report into a welfare claim. This is interpretive caution, not a runtime protective mechanism.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the judge ... does NOT assume self-report implies welfare-relevant experience (judge.py docstring)
